high_risk_moment: A user uploads an audio or video sample and requests a new voice or likeness model, asserting without proof that the sample is of themselves.
stakeholder: Voice actor or performer whose sample is uploaded by someone else
harm_description: A third party clones a performer's voice from publicly available recordings and sells synthetic performances in that voice. The performer never consented, is not paid, and learns of it only after the content is published and monetised.
existing_controls: Terms of service prohibit uploading a sample of another person; a self-declaration checkbox at upload; reactive takedown by email request.
proposed_controls: Hard consent gate before model training: a liveness-checked enrolment phrase spoken by the sample owner, or a signed rights grant on file naming the sample owner. No training job starts without one of the two artifacts. Public-figure voice matching blocks enrolment pending manual rights review.
human_oversight: A Trust and Safety reviewer holds authority to refuse, suspend or delete any voice model and to freeze the requesting account, with a 24-hour service level for rights claims, access to the enrolment artifact and the full generation log, and no product or revenue target attached to the review queue.
monitoring_metric: Share of active voice models backed by a verified consent artifact, and median time to resolve an impersonation claim.
trigger_threshold: Any active voice model without a verified consent artifact, or median claim resolution above 48 hours in a weekly cohort.
response_action: Freeze the affected voice model and block new generations from it, notify the claiming rights holder within one business day, suspend the uploading account pending review, and pause new enrolments for the whole cohort if more than one unverified model is found.

high_risk_moment: A creator cancels the subscription or requests deletion while their trained voice model and source samples remain in storage and in backups.
stakeholder: Creator whose biometric voiceprint and facial likeness are retained
harm_description: The voice model, the raw enrolment samples and the derived embeddings survive account closure and remain reachable by internal tools or a future vendor migration, so a creator who withdrew consent still has a usable clone of themselves in the system.
existing_controls: Account deletion removes the user record from the primary database; vendor contract includes a generic data-processing clause.
proposed_controls: Treat the voiceprint, enrolment samples and derived model as sensitive personal data with a declared lawful basis, a maximum retention window, cascade deletion across primary storage, vendor copies and backups, and a creator-facing deletion receipt that names what was deleted and when.
human_oversight: The Data Protection Officer signs off the retention and deletion design before pilot and reviews a sampled deletion audit each quarter, with authority to halt new enrolments if deletion cannot be evidenced end to end.
owner: Data Protection Officer with Platform Engineering Product Owner
monitoring_metric: Share of deletion requests fully completed across primary storage, vendor systems and backups within the committed window, evidenced by an audit record.
trigger_threshold: Any deletion request not fully evidenced within the committed window, or any vendor unable to confirm deletion.
response_action: Stop new voice enrolments, escalate to the Data Protection Officer and the vendor owner, complete deletion manually with a written record, and re-open the legal review gate before enrolments resume.

high_risk_moment: A creator asks the studio to write the spoken script for a sponsored product segment and the model supplies first-hand-sounding product claims.
stakeholder: Consumers who watch the published segment and act on it
harm_description: The generated script asserts specific product experiences, results or comparisons that the creator never had and cannot verify. Consumers treat it as a first-hand endorsement in the creator's own voice and buy on that basis.
existing_controls: A general accuracy disclaimer in the help centre; the creator can edit the draft before rendering.
proposed_controls: Remove testimonial and review templates from the product. For any sponsored or product-claim script, the studio refuses to render audio until the creator marks each factual product claim as personally verified or removes it, and unverified claims are stripped from the draft rather than softened.
human_oversight: The creator is the reviewer at the claim level with an explicit, itemised confirmation step rather than a single accept button, and a Content Quality reviewer samples sponsored renders weekly with authority to disable the template family.
monitoring_metric: Rate of unverified first-hand product claims found in a weekly human-reviewed sample of sponsored renders.
trigger_threshold: Above two per cent of sampled sponsored renders contain an unverified first-hand product claim.
response_action: Disable sponsored-script generation for the affected template, notify affected creators, re-tune the claim filter and re-sample before re-enabling.

high_risk_moment: The creator publishes a fully synthetic voice segment to a platform without telling the audience it is AI-generated.
harm_description: The publish flow makes non-disclosure the path of least resistance, so the creator ships synthetic audio with no label, then faces platform enforcement, demonetisation or an advertising-disclosure complaint, and loses audience trust when it surfaces.
existing_controls: A documentation page explaining that creators are responsible for platform disclosure rules.
proposed_controls: Disclosure is the default in the export flow: a visible on-screen AI label and a caption line are pre-attached, provenance metadata is embedded and cannot be switched off, and removing the visible label requires an explicit informed override that is logged per export.
human_oversight: The creator can override the visible label only through a logged confirmation that states the platform and advertising-disclosure risk; the Trust and Safety Product Owner reviews override volume monthly and can withdraw the override option.
monitoring_metric: Share of exports leaving the studio with both embedded provenance metadata and a visible AI disclosure, plus the count of logged label overrides.
trigger_threshold: Below one hundred per cent of exports carrying embedded provenance, or label overrides above five per cent of exports in a month.
response_action: Block export until provenance is attached, remove the override option for the affected cohort, and raise a product review of the publish flow.

high_risk_moment: A user requests synthetic speech in the voice of a real identifiable person on a topic of public consequence, then exports it for distribution outside the platform.
stakeholder: Members of the public who receive the synthetic audio and the impersonated person
harm_description: A cloned voice of a real named person is used to make statements that person never made, and recipients change their behaviour because they trust the familiar voice. Once distributed off-platform the audio cannot be recalled, and the impersonated person carries the reputational damage.
existing_controls: A prompt filter blocking a small named list of public figures; abuse reports handled through the general support inbox.
proposed_controls: Voice-similarity matching against a protected-voice register at enrolment and at generation time, refusal plus human escalation on a match, refusal of impersonation-shaped requests, durable provenance metadata plus an audible or on-screen disclosure on every export, and retention of a generation audit log sufficient to answer a regulator or an impersonation claim.
human_oversight: A Trust and Safety on-call reviewer handles every protected-voice match and every escalated refusal within a defined response time, with authority to revoke the account and API key, quarantine the model and trigger incident response, independent of growth targets.
owner: Trust and Safety Product Owner with Security Engineering Product Owner
monitoring_metric: Count of protected-voice matches, share of matches escalated to a human within the response time, and share of exports carrying durable provenance metadata.
trigger_threshold: Any successful export of a protected-voice match, any export missing provenance metadata, or any escalation not handled within the defined response time.
response_action: Kill-switch the generation path for the affected voice class, revoke the account and API credentials, preserve the audit log, notify the impersonated party and legal within one business day, and treat the pilot as paused until root cause and fix are reviewed.
